title: Highly Efficient Agrobacterium-Mediated Transformation of Tomato cv Micro-Tom From Cotyledon Explants
author: Débora Pagliuso
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: Solanum lycopersicum cv Micro-Tom Reagents 1. (NH 4 )NO 3 (ACS Cientifica, CAS number: R
Na 2 MoO 4 ·2H 2 O (Synth, CAS number: M1013.01.AE)
Na 2 EDTA·2H 2 O (Sigma-Aldrich, CAS number: E5134-1KG)

steps.title: Prepare stock solutions
steps.instruction: Make all required stock solutions, label, filter‑sterilize or autoclave as indicated, and store at the temperatures specified.

substeps.instruction: Solution A (macronutrients): dissolve 33 g (NH4)NO3, 38 g KNO3, 7.4 g MgSO4·7H2O, 3.4 g KH2PO4 in distilled water up to 1 L; keep at 4 °C (stable ≤2 months).
Solution B (calcium chloride): dissolve 8.8 g CaCl2·2H2O in water up to 1 L; keep at 4 °C (≤2 months).

Solution C (micronutrients): dissolve 1.24 g H3BO3, 3.38 g MnSO4·7H2O, 2.12 g ZnSO4·7H2O, 0.166 g KI, 0.05 g Na2MoO4·2H2O, 0.005 g CuSO4·5H2O, 0.005 g CoCl2·6H2O in water up to 1 L; keep at 4 °C (≤2 months).
Solution D (Fe‑EDTA): dissolve 2.78 g FeSO4·7H2O and 3.73 g Na2EDTA·2H2O in water up to 1 L; keep at 4 °C (≤2 months).
Vitamin mix: dissolve 0.05 g nicotinic acid (1 mg mL‑1), 0.05 g pyridoxine‑HCl (1 mg mL‑1), 0.5 g thiamine‑HCl (5 mg mL‑1), 5 g inositol (50 mg mL‑1) in water up to 50 mL; keep at 4 °C (≤2 months).
Acetosyringone: dissolve 196 mg in ethanol to 100 mM, bring volume to 10 mL, filter‑sterilize, aliquot, store at –20 °C (≤3 months).
Kanamycin: dissolve 1.25 g in water to 50 mg mL‑1, bring to 25 mL, filter‑sterilize, aliquot, store at –20 °C (≤3 months).
Meropenem: dissolve 1 g in water to 8.3 mg mL‑1, bring to 120 mL, filter‑sterilize, aliquot, store at –20 °C (≤3 months).
NAA (0.4 mM): dissolve 0.0074 g in water to 100 mL, add 1 M KOH drops to dissolve, filter‑sterilize (or autoclave), store at 4 °C (≤6 months).
BA (0.5 mM): dissolve 0.00225 g in water to 200 mL, add 1 N HCl drops to dissolve, filter‑sterilize, store at –20 °C (≤12 months).
Zeatin (1 mM): dissolve 0.0219 g in water to 100 mL, add 1 N HCl drops to dissolve, filter‑sterilize, store at –20 °C (≤6 months).
Peter’s 5× solution: dissolve 3.5 g Peters 20:20:20 (N:P:K) in water up to 1 L; dilute in tap water before use, keep at 4 °C, use within 1 week.

steps.title: Prepare plant culture media
steps.instruction: Prepare each culture medium using the stock solutions, adjust pH, add heat‑labile components after autoclaving, dispense into sterile plates or vessels, and store at 4 °C until use.

substeps.instruction: Germination medium (GM): mix 25 mL Solution A (2.5 % v/v), 25 mL Solution B (2.5 % v/v), 2.5 mL Solution C (0.25 % v/v), 5 mL Solution D (0.5 % v/v), 1 mL vitamin mix (0.1 % v/v), 15 g sucrose (1.5 % w/v), 2.3 g Phytagel (0.23 % w/v) in water up to 1 L; adjust pH to 5.8 with KOH, autoclave 121 °C 15 min 1.5 atm, dispense ~15 mL per 15 × 50 mm plate, store ≤2 weeks at 4 °C.

Virulence induction medium (VIM): combine 50 mL Solution A (5 % v/v), 50 mL Solution B (5 % v/v), 5 mL Solution C (0.5 % v/v), 10 mL Solution D (1 % v/v), 1 mL vitamin mix (0.1 % v/v), 30 g sucrose (3 % w/v), 6 g agar (0.6 % w/v); autoclave, cool partially, add 1 mL acetosyringone (100 mM) and 1 mL NAA (0.4 mM); adjust pH to 5.8, dispense ~15 mL per 15 × 50 mm plate, store ≤2 weeks at 4 °C.

Shoot‑inducing medium 1 (SIM‑1): mix 50 mL Solution A (5 % v/v), 50 mL Solution B (5 % v/v), 5 mL Solution C (0.5 % v/v), 10 mL Solution D (1 % v/v), 1 mL vitamin mix (0.1 % v/v), 30 g sucrose (3 % w/v), 6 g agar (0.6 % w/v); autoclave, cool, add 1 mL kanamycin (50 mg mL‑1, final 0.05 mg L‑1), 20 µL zeatin (0.5 mM, final 0.01 mM), 3.6 mL meropenem (8.3 mg mL‑1, final 0.03 mg L‑1), water to 1 L; adjust pH to 5.8, dispense ~15 mL per 15 × 50 mm plate, store ≤2 weeks at 4 °C.

Shoot‑inducing medium 2 (SIM‑2): same base as SIM‑1; add kanamycin 0.1 mg L‑1 (2.4 mL of 50 mg mL‑1), zeatin 0.003 mM (6 mL of 0.5 mM), meropenem 0.03 mg L‑1 (3.6 mL of 8.3 mg mL‑1); dispense ~40 mL per Magenta™ vessel, store ≤2 weeks at 4 °C.

Shoot‑inducing medium 3 (SIM‑3): same base as SIM‑1; add kanamycin 0.1 mg L‑1 (2.4 mL of 50 mg mL‑1), BA 0.005 mM (10 mL of 0.5 mM), meropenem 0.0075 mg L‑1 (0.9 mL of 8.3 mg mL‑1); dispense ~40 mL per Magenta™ vessel, store ≤2 weeks at 4 °C.

Root‑inducing medium (RIM): mix 25 mL Solution A (2.5 % v/v), 25 mL Solution B (2.5 % v/v), 2.5 mL Solution C (0.25 % v/v), 5 mL Solution D (0.5 % v/v), 1 mL vitamin mix (0.1 % v/v), 30 g sucrose (3 % w/v), 2.3 g Phytagel (0.23 % w/v); autoclave, cool, add meropenem 0.0075 mg L‑1 (0.9 mL of 8.3 mg mL‑1); adjust pH to 5.8, dispense ~40 mL per 15 × 100 mm plate, store ≤2 weeks at 4 °C.

Murashige & Skoog (MS) solution: combine 25 mL Solution A (2.5 % v/v), 25 mL Solution B (2.5 % v/v), 2.5 mL Solution C (0.25 % v/v), 5 mL water (0.5 % v/v); adjust pH to 5.8, keep at 4 °C (≤2 months).

Yeast extract peptone (YEP) medium: dissolve 10 g tryptone, 10 g yeast extract, 5 g NaCl, 9.6 g agar in water up to 1 L; adjust pH to 7.0 with NaOH, autoclave 121 °C 15 min 1.5 atm; dispense ~40 mL per 15 × 100 mm plate, store ≤2 weeks at 4 °C.

steps.title: Sterilize equipment and consumables
steps.instruction: Autoclave all glassware, micropipettes, tips, media, sieves and distilled water; heat‑sterilize spatula and tweezers by autoclaving or microbead sterilizer at 250 °C for 5 min.

steps.title: Surface-sterilize and germinate seeds
steps.instruction: Disinfect seeds with bleach/Tween solution, wash repeatedly, rest, then germinate on GM under controlled dark and light conditions.

substeps.instruction: In a 250 mL beaker add 80 mL sterile distilled water, 20 mL commercial bleach (2 % v/v) and three drops of Tween 20; homogenize.
Place the beaker on an orbital shaker inside the biosafety cabinet, agitate ~60 rpm for ~15 min.
Transfer seeds to a sterile metallic sieve, discard the bleach solution, and wash with ~100 mL sterile water on the shaker at ~60 rpm for ~5 min.
Repeat the wash nine additional times (total ten washes).
After the final wash let seeds rest in the water for ~30 min.
Remove excess water with the sieve and inoculate ~40 seeds into each sterile 15 × 50 mm Magenta™ vessel containing GM, spacing seeds ~0.5 cm apart.
Incubate vessels in the dark at 25 °C for 4 days.
Transfer vessels to light (12‑h photoperiod, ~50 µmol·m⁻²·s⁻¹, 25 ± 1 °C) for an additional 4 days.

steps.title: Cultivate Agrobacterium tumefaciens
steps.instruction: Grow the GV3101 strain on YEP with antibiotics, prepare pre‑inoculum and inoculum, then adjust bacterial density to OD 600 0.2‑0.3 in liquid GM.

substeps.instruction: Streak A. tumefaciens GV3101 on solid YEP medium supplemented with the appropriate antibiotics; incubate 28 ± 1 °C for 2 days to obtain isolated colonies.
Pick a single colony into 3 mL YEP + antibiotics; incubate 28 ± 1 °C, 180 rpm, in the dark for 18‑24 h (pre‑inoculum).
Add 100‑300 µL of the pre‑inoculum to each 250‑mL Erlenmeyer flask containing 50 mL YEP + antibiotics; incubate overnight under the same conditions.
Autoclave any remaining pre‑inoculum to inactivate it.
When the culture reaches OD 600 0.5‑0.7, centrifuge 3 000 × g for 10 min at room temperature (25 ± 1 °C).
Resuspend the pellet in liquid GM to obtain OD 600 0.2‑0.3; keep the suspension in the dark at room temperature while explants are prepared.

steps.title: Prepare cotyledon explants and co‑cultivate
steps.instruction: Excise cotyledon pieces, place them on VIM plates, inoculate with Agrobacterium suspension, and co‑incubate in the dark.

substeps.instruction: Using sterile tweezers and scissors, cut off both extremities of each cotyledon and make a transversal cut to obtain two pieces; keep the abaxial side facing down.
Place 40 explants onto each VIM plate, spacing ~2 mm; explants may be cut directly on the plate.
Add ~4 mL of the prepared A. tumefaciens suspension to each plate with a sterile pipette.
Incubate plates for 30 min in the dark at room temperature (no agitation).
Remove the bacterial suspension with fresh sterile tips and pipette.
Seal plates and incubate at 25 ± 1 °C in the dark for 2 days.

steps.title: Induce shoots on SIM‑1 medium
steps.instruction: Transfer co‑cultivated explants to SIM‑1 plates and maintain for four weeks under light to generate callus and initial shoots.

substeps.instruction: After the 2‑day co‑incubation, move explants to fresh SIM‑1 plates, ensuring the abaxial side contacts the medium.
Incubate at 25 ± 1 °C with a 12‑h photoperiod, ~50 µmol·m⁻²·s⁻¹ light for 2 weeks.
After 2 weeks, transfer explants to a new SIM‑1 plate and continue incubation for an additional 2 weeks.
Monitor for compact green‑brownish callus with meristematic domes (viable) versus necrotic tissue (non‑viable).

steps.title: Develop shoots on SIM‑2 medium
steps.instruction: Move healthy explants to SIM‑2 containing Magenta™ vessels and grow shoots to 1‑2 cm.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the regenerating explants to Magenta™ vessels containing 40 mL SIM‑2 medium.
Incubate under the same light (12 h, ~50 µmol·m⁻²·s⁻¹) and temperature (25 ± 1 °C) for 2‑3 weeks until shoots reach 1‑2 cm in length.

steps.title: Mature shoots on SIM‑3 medium
steps.instruction: Place 1‑2 cm shoots into SIM‑3 vessels and grow until 1‑3 fully expanded leaves appear.

substeps.instruction: Transfer shoots to Magenta™ vessels containing 40 mL SIM‑3 medium.
Continue culture under the same photoperiod and temperature until shoots develop 1‑3 leaves.

steps.title: Induce roots on RIM medium
steps.instruction: Excise shoots from callus, place them on RIM plates, and refresh medium bi‑weekly until roots >2 cm form.

substeps.instruction: Using a sterile scalpel, cut shoots away from residual callus tissue (cut base at 45° angle).
Transfer isolated shoots to Magenta™ vessels containing 40 mL RIM medium.
Every two weeks, transfer shoots to fresh RIM plates to maintain nutrient supply.
When roots longer than 2 cm appear, proceed to ex‑vitro hardening.

steps.title: Acclimate regenerated plants ex‑vitro
steps.instruction: Gradually harden rooted plants in vermiculite with MS solution, then transplant to substrate with fertilizers under greenhouse conditions.

substeps.instruction: Gently wash rooted plants in distilled water to remove medium residues.
Place one plant in each jar containing vermiculite saturated with MS nutrient solution; close the jar with its lid.
Maintain jars at 12‑h photoperiod, ~100 µmol·m⁻²·s⁻¹, 25 ± 1 °C for 3 weeks, watering routinely with MS solution.
Lid schedule: week 1 – lid fully closed; week 2 – open half of the lid; week 3 – remove lid completely.
After rooting, transplant each plant into a 250‑mL pot containing a 1:1 mix of commercial substrate and expanded vermiculite.
Amend the potting mix with 1 g L⁻¹ NPK 10:10:10, 4 g L⁻¹ dolomite limestone (MgCO₃ + CaCO₃), and 2 g L⁻¹ thermophosphate.
Cover pots with plastic cups (small holes) and 50 % shade cloth for the first week; remove covers after one week.
Grow plants under standard greenhouse conditions for seed production.

steps.title: Validate transgene by PCR
steps.instruction: Extract genomic DNA from regenerated leaves, set up PCR with specified reagents and cycling conditions, and analyze products on agarose gel.

substeps.instruction: Extract genomic DNA using the Edwards’ protocol (as cited).

Prepare PCR mix (per 25 µL reaction): 1× Taq buffer, 0.2 mM each dNTP, 1.5 mM MgCl₂, 0.5 µM forward primer (5′‑CTCTGATGTGGATAAGTTGTTC‑3′), 0.5 µM reverse primer (5′‑CTGAGAGTGGAGCCTTGGTG‑3′), 1 U Taq DNA polymerase, and 30 ng template DNA; add water to final volume.
Run thermocycler: 94 °C 5 min; 35 cycles of 94 °C 30 s, 55 °C 20 s, 72 °C 30 s; final extension 72 °C 5 min.
Separate PCR products on 1 % agarose gel at 90 V; include DNA ladder.
A 440 bp band indicates presence of the Cas9 transgene.
